newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives to turn right after election - poll.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives to turn right after election - poll.

text.p: The Conservative party seems likely to lurch to the right after the next general election, according to a poll in the Economist magazine.

Two thirds of prospective candidates in 75 seats where the sitting Conservative member of parliament is stepping down at the election took part in the survey. Forty percent of the retiring MPs also took part.

The Economist said the new candidates described themselves as far more sceptical on Europe than the retiring MPs and were far more strongly in favour of tax cuts, even if this meant cuts in public services.

It said the survey had to be treated with caution -- the sample of retiring MPs used to measure the change was small and may have had a left-wing bias, and it was not clear how many of the candidates would make it into parliament.
Separately, it found that Prime Minister John Major was the most popular choice among Conservative voters to lead the party if it lost the next election.
But when all voters were questioned in a poll, Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine came top, the magazine said.
Major got 27 percent backing from Conservative voters compared to 16 percent for Heseltine, but among all voters, Heseltine topped the poll with 16 percent to Major's 13 percent.

Conservative voters put former premier Margaret Thatcher third followed by John Redwood, the right-wing ex-minister who quit the cabinet to challenge Major for the leadership last year, and then Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke.
The general election is due in the next seven months and the Conservatives are tipped to lose to Labour.
